paper_metadata.title: Prediction of Stocks Index Price Using Quantum GANs

summary: The paper studies stock index prediction with a fully quantum GAN and a hybrid quantum-classical GAN on the AWS Braket SV1 simulator. The fully quantum model reports RMSE 571.36 (train) and 251.89 (test) after 5 epochs, while the classical GAN baseline is reported at 91.71 test RMSE; the hybrid model reports 49.88 train RMSE and 84.27 test RMSE after 150 epochs. The paper also notes that each FQGAN epoch took about 2 hours, with total simulation time exceeding 10 hours, and that amplitude embedding leads to exponentially scaling circuit depth.

experiments.description: Fully quantum GAN (FQGAN) for one-step stock index price forecasting using both quantum generator and quantum discriminator on AWS Braket SV1 simulator.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Amplitude embedding used to encode stock price time-series data into the quantum circuit; paper states qubit count follows ceil(log2 b) + ceil(log2 f) + 1 for past window size b and future window size f.

problem_instance.description: Stock index price prediction using historical market data; one-step forecast with past window size 3 days to predict the next day.
problem_instance.dataset_name: NIFTY index / stock index price data

dataset_specification.preprocessing: historical stock index price data; min-max scaling implied by invertible FQGAN normalization discussion

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Data prepared for invertible FQGAN; amplitude embedding; min-max scaling and inverse min-max transform used for normalization factor recovery in the invertible variant.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compared training and test RMSE; results reported for 5 epochs on AWS SV1 simulator.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Historical market data prepared with amplitude embedding; invertible FQGAN uses overlapping input/output windows to estimate normalization factor.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: RMSE computed on train/test predictions; inverse min-max transform applied to recover price scale.
implementation_details.total_execution_time: Each epoch took about 2 hours; total simulation time exceeded 10 hours for 5 epochs.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper claims quantum advantage qualitatively, but no asymptotic or quantified speedup is demonstrated for the FQGAN experiment. The text notes long simulator runtime and inability to test on real hardware.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No practical advantage demonstrated; the fully quantum GAN is only evaluated on a simulator and has worse RMSE than the classical baseline.
limiting_factors: Classical baseline RMSE 91.71 is far better than FQGAN test RMSE 251.89
